text: The cloud base is 650 feet AGL. What maximum altitude preserves 500 feet of vertical clearance below the cloud?

choices.explanation: Incorrect. “400 feet AGL” is the normal Part 107 altitude limit, but flying at 400 feet under a 650-foot cloud base would leave only 250 feet of vertical separation—short of the required 500 feet.
Incorrect. “500 feet AGL” would leave only 150 feet below a 650-foot cloud base. The rule requires 500 feet below the cloud, not a 500-foot flight altitude.
Correct. “150 feet AGL” preserves the required clearance because 650 feet − 500 feet = 150 feet AGL.

teachingExplanation: This is a short subtraction problem. The cloud base is 650 feet AGL, and Part 107 requires the drone to remain at least 500 feet below the cloud. Subtract the required clearance from the cloud base: 650 − 500 = 150 feet AGL. That means 150 feet AGL is the highest altitude that still preserves the required 500-foot vertical separation. The 400-foot general altitude limit does not help here because the cloud creates a lower usable ceiling. When weather and the normal altitude limit both apply, the lower limit is the one that actually controls.
howToSolve: Write the two numbers before looking at the choices. Cloud base = 650 feet AGL; required vertical clearance below cloud = 500 feet. 650 − 500 = 150 feet AGL, so 150 feet is the highest altitude that preserves the required clearance.
memoryTip: Cloud clearance math: cloud base minus 500 feet.
reviewPrompt: If the cloud base were 900 feet AGL, what would be the highest altitude that preserves 500 feet below the cloud?
